13.27 Permutation symmetry of component marginals
The merge-moment argument in [ Ope26b, Section 7] uses permutation invariance of an auxiliary
marginal obtained by tracing other registers. The following partial-trace identities do not require
a product state or normalization.

13.28 The actual good auxiliary marginal
The auxiliary symmetry needed for the merge moments is a symmetry of the actual reduced
matrix. It follows from the simultaneous symmetry of the excitation component after every
discarded register is traced out.

Theorem 13.28.3 (Permutation invariance of the good auxiliary marginal) . Lean ✓ Stmt In

Proof. ✓ Proof Extend a permutation of the good copies by the identity on 𝐵. The chosen coor-
dinate equivalences give an actual permutation of all 𝑘 copies that fixes every excited coordinate.
The stabilizer identity therefore shows that 𝑤 is fixed by its simultaneous physical, auxiliary and
exterior action. Under the actual coordinate regrouping, this action is the tensor product of a
permutation of the discarded register and the given permutation of 𝐶𝑚. Both factors are unitary.
Partial-trace covariance then proves that the reduced matrix commutes with the retained action.
Interchanging the finite trace sums identifies this reduced matrix with the two successive traces
in the definition.
This proves the auxiliary permutation invariance used after [ Ope26b, Section 7, equation
(comparator:merge-moments)]. It does not assert that the auxiliary copies are independent or
establish the merge-moment estimate.
13.29 A controlled overlap on the physical buffer
All registers in this section have arbitrary finite bases. Their dimensions may differ, and the

space is nonzero.
